beats.hook: The man outside my window had been standing there for three nights in a row — and he was wearing my dead father's coat.
beats.setup: I was 24, living alone in a rented house in rural Ohio. My dad had passed eight months earlier.
beats.incident: The first night I thought it was a shadow. The second night I turned on the porch light. He was just — standing at the tree line. Still. Facing the house. I told myself it was a neighbor. Then I remembered — I had buried my dad in that coat.
beats.escalation: I called my sister. She went quiet for a long time. Then she said our mom had donated a bag of Dad's clothes to the thrift store two weeks after the funeral. Without telling anyone. That coat could have been in that bag.
beats.payoff: I drove to the tree line the next morning. There was nothing there. No footprints. No broken branches. Nothing. But there was one thing — a single button. Dark brown. Vintage. I recognized it immediately. It was from that coat.
beats.cta: I still have the button. I've never gone back to that house. What would you have done — stayed, or left and never looked back?
